chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: From Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub bin Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali bin Ismail bin Ammar, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban bin Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I sit in the Masjid, and people come and ask me questions; if I do not answer them, they do not accept from me, and I dislike answering them with your verdicts and what has come from you (i.e., Shia sources), so he (peace be upon him) said to me: Look at what you know is from their own verdicts and inform them about that.

key_terms.أَبَانَ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ: Aban bin Taghlib, a prominent narrator
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: The Mosque, a place of gathering and teaching

ai.seo_question: How should one answer non-Shia people regarding religious matters if their own sources are accepted by them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Rijal al-Kashi*, Aban bin Taghlib seeks guidance from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the dilemma of being rejected by the general public when citing specific Shia sources. The Imam advises him to present the verdicts as those of the Imams generally, rather than specifying the source, to ensure the answers are accepted. This highlights the early Shia scholarly strategy of *taqiyya* and pragmatic communication to establish religious authority within the broader Muslim community.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/116] Rijal al-Kashshi: From Hamduwayh from Ya`qub bin Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ali bin Ismail bin Ammar from Ibn Muskan from Aban bin Taghlib who said:

I said to Abi Abdillah عليه السلام: I do sit in the Masjid – and the people come and ask me questions, so if I do not answer them they do not accept from me (i.e. they insist on answers), and I dislike answering them based on your verdicts and according to what has come from you (i.e. since they are not Shia), so he عليه السلام said to me: look at what you know is from their own verdicts and inform them about that (i.e. answer them using their own sources and scholars).
